{{nowrap|Clausura: [[Darío Cvitanich]] (13 goals)}} | biggest home win = | biggest away win = | highest scoring = | matches player = | total goals = | average goals = | longest wins = | longest unbeaten = | longest losses = | prevseason = [[2006–07 Argentine Primera División|2006–07]] | nextseason = [[2008–09 Argentine Primera División season|2008–09]] }} The Apertura 2007 saw much success for the smaller teams in Argentine football. The eventual champions [[Club Atlético Lanús|Lanús]] won the title for the first time in their history, the first maiden champions since [[Argentinos Juniors]] in [[1984 in Argentine football|1984]]. Second place went to [[Club Atlético Tigre|Tigre]], a club playing their first season in the [[Argentine Primera]] since 1980 and making their best finish ever in the top flight. Third place went to [[Club Atlético Banfield|Banfield]], completing an extremely unlikely top three. Another small club, [[Arsenal de Sarandí|Arsenal]] won the [[Copa Sudamericana 2007|2007]] [[Copa Sudamericana]], the first major title in their history, making them the first Argentine club other than [[Boca Juniors]] to win an international competition since [[San Lorenzo de Almagro|San Lorenzo]] won the [[Copa Sudamericana 2002]]. Another feature of the Apertura was the number of managerial changes, by the end of the Apertura there had been 12 [[2007-08 in Argentine football#Managerial Changes|managerial changes]]. The Clausura 2008 was won by [[Club Atlético River Plate|River Plate]], their first title since 2004.{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/2008/06/08/mas_futbol/1212876018_850215.html|title=River Plate se proclama campeón del torneo Clausura 2008|work=[[Diario AS]]|agency=[[EFE]]|date=8 June 2008|access-date=22 June 2025|language=es}} For the first time the 380 games of the season were broadcast live on television. ==Club locations== {{Location map+ |Argentina Greater Buenos Aires |float=right |width=325 |caption=Locations of the '''2007−08 Primera División''' teams within [[Greater Buenos Aires]] |places= {{Location map~ |Argentina Greater Buenos Aires |lat=-34.606105 |long=-58.472612 |label=
